pr_body: This PR changes `pr view` and `issue view` to no longer display minimized comments, instead they now show small headers indicating why a comment has been minimized. After chatting with @ampinsk we decided that the minimized headers should be white, not gray, as the original design proposed. closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2847

issue_context.title: Hidden comments on conversation timelines are still shown
issue_context.body:
In threads where comments are minimized due to being marked as spam, or off topic, are still shown in the CLI with no indication that they were hidden on the web, or why. 

**Questions**
- How should we hide these comments? 
- Should we offer a way to display them? 
- What are all the cases where comments are hidden, and how should we display them being "minimized"?
comments:
Great catch! Thanks for raising these questions.

> * How should we hide these comments?

I vote to render some sort of header that indicates that a comment was here but that it's been minimized, to mimic web behavior.

> * Should we offer a way to display them?

I do not think so. It would be technically hard to allow “expanding” them individually. I think interacting with potentially harmful content is best suited for the web right now where there are more moderation and content reporting tools available.

> * What are all the cases where comments are hidden, and how should we display them being "minimized"?

The web interface renders them like so: `{user avatar} This comment has been minimized. {show button}`. I can imagine us rendering the same sentence without the avatar or expand button, of course.

These types of comments can be minimized, per our API: IssueComment (includes PR comments), CommitComment, PullRequestReviewComment, GistComment.
All of ☝️ sounds very reasonable to me. Thanks @ampinsk and @mislav!
